item.title: Open-Source AI Attribution Index, 2026 Q3: Only 13.2% of Commits Disclose AI, and That Is Too Low
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: Almost every developer I know writes code with AI, yet in 20 large open-source projects only 13.2% of 2026 Q3 commits disclose it, and Rust, Kubernetes and Django are near zero. Many people use AI and don’t say so. My view: maintainers shouldn’t ask whether AI wrote a change, but whether the contributor can stand behind it. Disclosing is still the better habit.

item.title: Who Writes Open Source? What the Commit Addresses of 107 Projects Say
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: Counting 446,000 commits made to 107 large open-source projects in the last year by the domain of the author’s email: 29% came from organization addresses, but the median project is at 16%. Company projects and community projects differ widely; Google committed to 40 of them in a year, and a fifth of all commits don’t say where they come from.

item.title: gitstats Upgrade Arrives—JSON Output, Cross-Platform Compatibility, and Code Refactoring!
item.author: xianpeng.shen@gmail.com (Xianpeng Shen)
item.description: After two months of continuous improvement, gitstats now supports JSON output, code refactoring, argparse replacing getopt, and full compatibility with Windows and macOS. Welcome to use and Star support!

item.title: Reviving GitStats — Breathing New Life into Git History Analysis

item.description: This post details the revival of the GitStats project, including its migration to Python 3, the creation of a modern CI/CD pipeline, publication to PyPI and Docker, and future improvement plans.
